note: OPIc 롤플레이 3단계(질문하기, 문제 해결, 관련 경험)용 틀. 세부 내용은 자기 상황에 맞게 바꿔 쓴다. 3번은 오사카 여행 이야기(S1)를 재활용한다.

scripts.title: 1. Asking Questions
scripts.question: You want to book a hotel for your next trip. Call the hotel and ask three or four questions about the rooms and services.
scripts.original:
Hi, I'm calling because I'd like to book a room for my next trip. I have a few questions, if you don't mind.
First of all, do you have any rooms available from the 20th to the 23rd? I'm traveling with my family, so we need a room for three people.
Second, how much is it per night, and is breakfast included?
Also, I heard there's a hot spring near your hotel. Is it inside the hotel, or do we have to go outside?
Lastly, is there a parking lot? We're planning to rent a car.
Thank you so much for your help. I'll call you back after I talk to my family.

scripts.title: 2. Solving a Problem
scripts.question: When you arrive at the hotel, they say your reservation does not exist. Explain the situation to the front desk and offer two or three alternatives.
scripts.original:
Excuse me, I think there's a problem. I booked a room on your website two weeks ago, but you said my reservation doesn't exist.
Here's my confirmation email. As you can see, I already paid with my credit card.
I'm really tired after a long flight, so I hope we can solve this quickly. I have a few ideas.
First, if you have any other room tonight, I'm okay with a smaller one.
Second, if the hotel is fully booked, could you find me a room at a hotel nearby?
Lastly, if neither works, please give me a full refund, and I'll look for another place myself.
I'd really appreciate your help.
keywords: booked two weeks ago, no reservation
first: another room, smaller is okay

scripts.title: 3. Related Experience
scripts.question: Have you ever had a problem while you were traveling? Tell me what happened and how you solved it.
scripts.original:
Actually, I had a problem during my trip to Osaka last summer.
On the second night, my family and I went to Dotonbori, and I ate way too much takoyaki. A few hours later, I got a terrible stomachache.
It was late at night, and I couldn't read Japanese, so I didn't know what medicine to buy.
So I asked the front desk for help. They told me about a drugstore nearby, and I bought some medicine there.
After that, I rested in the hot spring at the hotel, and I felt much better the next morning.
Since then, I always carry some basic medicine when I travel abroad.
keywords: late at night, couldn't read Japanese
